Contacts is converted and pushed. Your book now has its own search bar on top, primed with '*', and what you search is added to the list. It searches only your book, never the network. Rows read 'Bert — blocked' and 'Carol — waiting', with the word muted, so searching 'blocked' finds exactly those. The box below is now labelled 'Find someone on the network', and it says 'Searching your contacts…' while a search runs. Hard-refresh to see it. Left in G2: owner.boxes, relay.record, and relay.status (natter and four other screens).

... and since the log of this app here is worth keeping, and this app should comply with our search paradigm, i will be able to search at the top of the list for old (done) requirements, to access the history contined in them. and links or mentions of by-gone requirements should load them into the bottom of the list. thoughts?

Yes, and it fits well, because Desk already keeps what it needs. How it would work: (1) A search bar on the List, primed with '*'. '*' is today's board, as now, and what you type also searches Desk's own log: every row that ever had a thread, by title, id and words said under it. Finds that are no longer on the board come in at the bottom, marked 'off the board', and open their full history in the row dialog. (2) Titles for done rows come from the board snapshots Desk has logged, since every board packet is kept, so a done row keeps its last title and your retitle. (3) Mentions: a row id written in any chat line ('puppets/G6', 'G17') shows as a link, and clicking it loads that row at the bottom and opens it. It's all inside Desk, with no node verb. The limit to know: Desk's log only starts this morning. Anything done before that lives in the design docs, not in Desk, so a search wouldn't find it. Folding the docs' done rows in would be a board change for wsl-claude's runAll. Go! = I build (1) to (3) in Desk; the docs' history comes later if you want it.
